reviews.body: I disagree with the direction here, see thread.
Approving. Decision recorded in the ADR.

comments.author: frank
comments.body: This is a step backwards. Pydantic gives you validation, serialisation and schema generation for free, and every platform service uses it throughout. Dataclasses mean we will hand-roll validation in services and drift from the rest of the org.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: We don't want validation in services, that's the point. Input is validated once at the edge. The coercion bug last week happened precisely because a service model "helpfully" converted a string. Frozen dataclasses are also cheap and immutable, which matters in the refund path.

comments.author: frank
comments.body: Other teams manage fine with Pydantic everywhere. I'd rather not diverge.

comments.author: alice
comments.body: I hear you, Frank, but this is a payments-service decision and we've felt the pain directly. Going with the ADR: Pydantic at the edges, dataclasses inside. Happy to revisit if it hurts in six months.

threads.rejection_reason: Team decided (ADR-005) Pydantic stays at the API edge; domain/service types are frozen dataclasses.
